source.title: Judging Adam: Studying the Performance of Optimization Methods on ML4SE Tasks
source.authors: D. Pasechnyuk; Anton Prazdnichnykh; Mikhail Evtikhiev; Timofey Bryksin

record.tranche_reason: Extends optimizer comparisons to code-related generation tasks and reports held-out task scores, but does not measure train–test gaps or test the claim’s other versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports optimizer task scores and rankings, not training error, so it cannot establish whether optimizer choice changes the training–test gap. Its optimizer comparisons bear on V4’s held-out-performance component. Other versions are not tested.
record.test_reason: Table I directly compares adaptive optimizers with SGD and momentum on held-out code-to-text performance, extending V4 to a new setting. Training scores are unnecessary for testing V4's held-out-performance component, although their absence prevents assessing performance at matched training loss.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors find substantial optimizer-dependent score differences, identify RAdam/LaRAdam as best overall, and report greater ranking variation across models than datasets. They recommend LaRAdam as the first choice and RAdam as a fallback, while acknowledging the absence of hyperparameter tuning.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares optimizers on source-code generation tasks and reports task scores; it does not reproduce the original generalization-gap experiments or report training error.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported optimizer ranking depends on model choice; optimizer performance also varies across model–dataset combinations.

fits_no_version.finding: RAdam or its Lookahead modification outperforms Adam in 14 of 16 model–dataset combinations; optimizer rankings vary more across models than across datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive optimizer variants differ in held-out performance on code-to-text tasks under default hyperparameters.

record.peer_reviewed: 2023 IEEE/ACM 45th International Conference on Software Engineering: New Ideas and Emerging Results (ICSE-NIER)
record.problems: No training scores are reported, so the generalization gap cannot be assessed. Hyperparameters were not tuned; the authors describe the study as a pilot with a two-step optimizer filtration scheme. The tested tasks and models are limited, and models were of similar size.
record.rows_left_out: The optimizer score tables report many model–dataset–optimizer combinations, but they do not report training error and therefore cannot measure the generalization gap named in V4. No rows were extracted.

untested.parts: Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Training performance; learning-rate and schedule tuning; broader tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching to SGD; image classification and word-level language modeling.
Batch-size effects under controlled training budgets.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: There are no extracted rows to fix. The stated reason for excluding all score tables is incorrect: V4 includes held-out optimizer comparisons without requiring training-error measurements. Table I's direct adaptive-versus-SGD comparisons should be extracted. These omissions are already declared in rows_left_out, so missing is empty. Comparisons among adaptive methods alone do not establish V4's adaptive-versus-SGD claim. A common learning rate within each architecture and no optimizer-specific tuning limit the interpretation.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Network width beyond interpolation and test error.

Training performance versus held-out performance; image-classification and language benchmarks; broader hyperparameter tuning; the reported effects of decoupled weight decay or switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language models.
Batch size and training duration effects.
Sharpness and other measured properties as predictors of the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

relationships.condition: Java documentation generation with TreeLSTM, CodeGNN, and CodeTransformer, using fixed learning rates and default optimizer hyperparameters.
relationships.reason: Text-only evidence from Table I: Adam exceeds both SGD and momentum in chrF: TreeLSTM 20.7 versus 19.8/20.0; CodeGNN 23.0 versus 22.4/22.6; CodeTransformer 34.8 versus 0.2/12.8. Adaptive methods therefore need not perform worse in this untuned code-task setting; no extracted row ids exist.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly exceeded SGD and momentum in chrF across these models, but the comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Java documentation generation with Code2Seq, using fixed learning rates and default optimizer hyperparameters.
relationships.reason: Text-only evidence from Table I: Adam's chrF is 19.5 versus SGD's 13.7 and momentum's 19.7, while RAdam reaches 22.9. The comparison depends on which adaptive optimizer and SGD variant are chosen; no extracted row ids exist.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly exceeded SGD but slightly trailed momentum while RAdam scored higher, but these comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
